2607.13034.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
2607.13034.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate multi-step engineering and informatics workflows, yet they rarely ask how much effort a task actually requires. They often follow a maximum-context-first strategy--re-reading files and dependencies they have already seen--turning a one-line edit into a small code-base audit. We argue the missing capability is task-aware execution-scope estimation: judging a task's difficulty, the information it truly needs, and the shortest reliable path before committing budget. We formalize minimum-sufficient execution and the Agent Cognitive Redundancy Ratio (ACRR), and propose E3 (Estimate, Execute, Expand): the agent estimates an initial operating point, executes a minimum viable path, and expands scope only when verification fails. On MSE-Bench--a deterministic benchmark of 121 edits in a capability-controlled simulator--E3 matches the strongest baseline's 100% success while cutting cost by 85%, tokens by 91%, and inspected files by 92%, and further beats a strong adaptive retrieval baseline by 16%; the gains survive held-out instruction wording and essentially every cost weighting. A companion real-model harness (LLM-Case) corroborates the effect on a live gpt-4o agent editing a real open-source library, with every candidate patch graded by actually running the project's real pytest suite against a measured oracle: the over-reading is milder but real, and E3 is the leanest and fastest policy at comparable task success--its one shortfall a provider rate-limit, not a wrong edit. We frame this as a controlled probe of execution redundancy, not a measurement of any deployed agent, and position task-aware execution as a step toward engineering-grounded AI (EGAI)--agents whose effort is anchored in the engineering reality of the task. We release the framework and benchmark.
2607.13034.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）代理越來越多地自動化多步驟的工程和資訊工作流程，但它們很少詢問一項任務實際需要多少努力。<lb/>它們通常遵循最大上下文優先的策略——重新閱讀它們已經看過的文件和依賴項——將一行編輯變成小型代碼庫的審計。<lb/>我們認為缺失的能力是任務感知的執行範圍估算：評估任務的難度、它真正需要的信息，以及在分配預算之前的最短可靠路徑。<lb/>我們形式化了最小充分執行和代理認知冗餘比率（ACRR），並提出E3（估算、執行、擴展）：代理估算初始操作點，執行最小可行路徑，並僅在驗證失敗時擴展範圍。<lb/>在MSE-Bench——一個在能力受控模擬器中進行的121次編輯的確定性基準測試——E3與最強基線的100%成功率相匹配，同時將成本降低85%、標記數降低91%、檢查的文件數降低92%，並進一步超越一個強大的自適應檢索基線16%；這些增益在保留的指令措辭和幾乎所有成本權重下依然有效。<lb/>一個伴隨的實時模型工具（LLM-Case）證實了其對一個實時gpt-4o代理編輯真實開源庫的影響，每個候選補丁都通過實際運行項目的真實pytest套件對照測量的預言者進行評估：過度閱讀較輕但真實，E3是與相似任務成功率相比最精簡和最快的策略——其唯一的短板是供應商速率限制，而不是錯誤編輯。<lb/>我們將此框架視為執行冗餘的受控探測，而不是對任何已部署代理的測量，並將任務感知的執行定位為朝向以工程為基礎的人工智慧（EGAI）邁進的一步——那些努力根植於任務的工程現實中的代理。<lb/>我們發布了該框架和基準測試。
